tasks.spec: ROLE: fix worker for the Mott booking gateway, lane 40 (authoritative user_text availability semantics). Work entirely inside your current working directory; never modify anything outside CWD; no network, no git commits, no MCP/Apps/skills, no deploys. CONTEXT - measured live with a clean A/B probe against the production /availability endpoint minutes ago: with identical explicit from='in 2 weeks', the request returns 08/18/2026 slots when user_text is also 'in 2 weeks', but returns TODAY's (08/04) slots when user_text carries the raw patient sentence "I'm leaving town today and won't be back for 2 weeks about then?" - the gateway's authoritative user_text interpretation overrides the explicit from/to and its sentence scanner latches the word 'today'. The pathway extraction layer is now proven correct (it sends from='in 2 weeks'); the gateway's own sentence interpreter is the last wrong layer. DESIGN DECISION (do not re-litigate): the authoritative user_text layer STAYS authoritative - do not flip precedence to from/to - instead teach the interpreter availability semantics so every caller benefits. BASE FILE: ./deployed-bland_gateway.py in CWD is BYTE-EQUAL to what is running in production right now as image mott-lane-39 (it was byte-verified during that deploy). Work on a copy named ./fixed-bland_gateway.py; keep every existing line unless the fix requires changing it; keep the diff minimal and in-style. TASK: (1) Locate the authoritative user_text interpretation path for /availability (the code that resolves a date from the free-text sentence and overrides/fills from/to) and cite file location plus line range in DEBUG-GW40.md. (2) Extend it with availability semantics: when the sentence contains a departure/unavailability construction - patterns like 'leaving (town )?(today|tomorrow|on X)', 'going away', 'out of town', 'gone (for|until)', "won't be back (for|until) X", 'back in X', 'not (back|around|available) (for|until) X' - the resolved date must be the RETURN/availability period: for '(for|in) N days/weeks/months' constructions resolve today+offset (reuse the existing resolve_relative_date offset logic - do not duplicate it); for 'until <date>' resolve that date; the departure date itself ('today' in the canonical sentence) must never be chosen when such a construction is present. Sentences without departure constructions keep their existing interpretation exactly. (3) Add unit tests beside the existing suite covering at least: the canonical sentence above resolving to today+14; "I'm out of town until the 18th" resolving to the 18th; 'gone for 10 days' resolving to today+10; regression: 'today', 'tomorrow', 'thursday please', 'in 2 weeks', and one explicit date keep current behavior. Use the frozen/injected-today pattern the lane-39 tests use. (4) Build a scratch test tree inside CWD: copy /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGW39b/gw-datetime-tolerance/gw to ./gwtest, install fixed-bland_gateway.py as ./gwtest/container/bland_gateway.py, add your new tests, run the FULL suite green. (5) Write ./proof_intent.py: standalone, imports from ./gwtest, no network; for each case prints exactly one line 'CASE=<label> DATE=YYYY-MM-DD': away-sentence (the canonical sentence, expect today+14), until-18th ("I'm out of town until the 18th", expect this month's or next month's 18th as the existing date logic resolves it - print what the parser returns), gone-10-days ('gone for 10 days', expect today+10), plain-today ('I can come in today', expect today), thursday ('thursday please', expect next thursday's date). (6) DEBUG-GW40.md: the A/B evidence, interpreter location, the change, test commands with output tails, and the note that deploy is separately gated. Leave everything uncommitted.
tasks.check: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 ./proof_intent.py > proof.out 2>&1 || { echo 'FAIL: proof_intent crashed'; tail -6 proof.out; exit 1; }; exp14=$(python3 -c "import datetime;print((datetime.date.today()+datetime.timedelta(days=14)).isoformat())"); exp10=$(python3 -c "import datetime;print((datetime.date.today()+datetime.timedelta(days=10)).isoformat())"); today=$(python3 -c "import datetime;print(datetime.date.today().isoformat())"); grep -q "CASE=away-sentence DATE=$exp14" proof.out || { echo "FAIL: away-sentence did not resolve to $exp14"; cat proof.out; exit 1; }; grep -q "CASE=gone-10-days DATE=$exp10" proof.out || { echo 'FAIL: gone-10-days case'; cat proof.out; exit 1; }; grep -q "CASE=plain-today DATE=$today" proof.out || { echo 'FAIL: plain-today regressed'; cat proof.out; exit 1; }; grep -qE 'CASE=thursday DATE=[0-9-]+' proof.out || { echo 'FAIL: thursday case missing'; cat proof.out; exit 1; }; diffcount=$(python3 -c "import difflib;a=open('deployed-bland_gateway.py').readlines();b=open('fixed-bland_gateway.py').readlines();print(sum(1 for l in difflib.unified_diff(a,b) if l.startswith(('+','-')) and not l.startswith(('+++','---'))))"); [ "$diffcount" -lt 220 ] || { echo "FAIL: diff too large ($diffcount changed lines) - not minimal"; exit 1; }; cd gwtest && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q > ../pytest.out 2>&1; rc=$?; cd ..; summary=$(tail -1 pytest.out); [ $rc -eq 0 ] || { echo "FAIL: suite red: $summary"; tail -12 pytest.out; exit 1; }; echo "$summary" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+ passed' || { echo "FAIL: pytest summary not clean: $summary"; exit 1; }; grep -qi 'user_text' DEBUG-GW40.md || { echo 'FAIL: DEBUG-GW40.md lacks interpreter documentation'; exit 1; }; echo "PASS: availability semantics proven offline - $summary"
tasks.verified: The gateway's authoritative sentence interpreter resolves departure constructions to the patient's return period (canonical away-sentence to today+14, gone-for-N to today+offset) while plain phrases keep exact current behavior - proven by executing the interpreter and the full suite against a minimal diff on the byte-true deployed lane-39 file.
